claim: For the binary LCD code \(C\) of parameters \([57,8,25]_2\) displayed by Lim, An, and Kim (arXiv:2609.02096v1), expand each hexadecimal digit into four binary digits in most-significant-bit-first order and delete the three appended zero columns. Among all \(\binom{57}{2}=1596\) double punctures of this displayed representative, exactly four coordinate pairs—\(\{9,18\}\), \(\{10,30\}\), \(\{34,48\}\), and \(\{41,42\}\), with coordinates numbered from \(1\)—produce an LCD code of minimum distance \(24\). Hence a binary LCD \([55,8,24]_2\) code exists. Since the general binary linear-code bound gives \(d(55,8)=24\), it follows that \(d_{\mathrm{LCD}}(55,8)=24\). This improves the value \(23\) reached at length \(55\), dimension \(8\), in the source's reported shortest-embedding experiments to the sharp bound \(24\).

integrity.proof_basis: Exact finite-field row reduction plus exhaustive enumeration of all 1596 double punctures and all 256 words per dimension-eight row span.
integrity.source_reconstruction: The source hexadecimal matrix is independently reconstructed and checked to have rank 8, LCD Gram rank 8, and minimum distance 25 before puncturing.
integrity.unproved_limits: No equivalence classification of all optimal LCD codes is claimed.

scientific_limitations: The calculation classifies double punctures only of the displayed \([57,8,25]_2\) representative, not all equivalent or inequivalent representatives.
It does not classify all LCD \([55,8,24]_2\) codes.
A residual bibliographic risk remains for poorly indexed prior constructions.
title: Double puncturing settles \(d_{\mathrm{LCD}}(55,8)=24\)
